messages:
alex: Quick follow-up from the RFC review: proposing a compact, low-cardinality 'request_class' + optional 'cost_hint' propagation header for traces/metrics/logs. Goal is cheaper cost attribution without exploding cardinality.

maria: this feels promising. can you sketch how it flows across async boundaries? like kafka, lambda, db triggers?

alex: flow sketch: request enters -> front proxy assigns request_class (one of service-defined enums) and cost_hint (small int bucket). header names: X-RWI-Req-Class, X-RWI-Cost-Hint. downstream services copy on outgoing calls. async messages embed the same fields in envelope metadata.

pranay: worried about `request_class` becoming high-cardinality over time if teams add values. need guardrails.

alex: agreed. plan: enforce enum registration in schema repo + CI check that new values are approved and mapped to cost buckets. default unknown -> 'unclassified' which maps to a conservative cost bucket.

sam: how do we use this in observability backends? do we join traces->metrics at ingest time or tag metrics during processing?

alex: two-tier approach: 1) at trace ingest, surface request_class as a top-level tag for sampling and low-cardinality rollups; 2) metrics pipeline will map cost_hint -> cost estimate per-op and emit aggregated cost_by_request_class counters. avoid tagging high-cardinality fields on metric series.

jess-bot: automated note: this change will require: schema update, kafka envelope contract bump, agent SDK patch, and a rollout plan.

dan: curious about query ergonomics for product teams. If I want cost for a feature, will I be searching by request_class?

alex: yes, product teams should pick a stable request_class per feature. if they need finer granularity, they can add internal annotations (kept out of metric series) and use trace-level ad-hoc analysis.

maria: sampling implications? If we sample traces aggressively, we might miss small but expensive outliers. cost_hint helps here: high cost_hint forces higher sampling rate and retention of full traces.

pranay: can you show example headers + envelope json for async? small snippet pls.

alex: sure:```http
X-RWI-Req-Class: signup-flow
X-RWI-Cost-Hint: 3
```async envelope example:```json
{"envelope": {"meta": {"request_class": "signup-flow", "cost_hint": 3}, "payload": {...}}}
```

sam: how do we map cost_hint values to dollars or GPU-seconds? who owns the mapping?

alex: infra (pricing team) owns base mapping per op type. default mapping table living in optimize service with versioned config. cost_hint is intentionally coarse (0-5). teams can request bucket adjustments via infra PR.

dan: what about cardinality drift guard? Maybe auto-alert when new request_class appears in >X unique values per week?

pranay: +1 to auto-alert. also require a lint rule in SDK to reject freeform request_class strings unless explicitly enabled.

maria: rollout plan proposal: 1) schema + SDK update in canary services 2) kafka envelope contract bump and consumer compatibility tests 3) two-week shadow tagging in metrics pipeline 4) enable cost_by_request_class aggregates 5) opt-in forced sampling for cost_hint>=4 6) docs + onboarding checklist for product teams.

alex: that matches my thoughts. add: backfill policy — we won't backfill historical traces with request_class; instead we'll provide an attribution best-effort using trace heuristics for a 30d window.

sam: worth noting: some internal infra calls are high cardinality by nature (user_id, dataset_id). ensure those never get promoted into request_class space.

pranay: action items?

alex: I will open a lightweight schema PR with the header names + enum registry doc. maria, can you draft the kafka envelope changes? pranay, can you add the SDK lint check? sam, coordinate mapping with pricing. jess-bot, add checklist tasks and link to rollout doc.

jess-bot: created tasks: #OBS-reqclass-schema, #OBS-kafka-envelope, #OBS-sdk-lint, #OBS-costmap-infra. links: https://go/r/OBS-reqclass-schema (internal).

dan: thanks — please add a short blurb for privacy/security team: make sure request_class doesn't encode PII.

maria: noted. will include a privacy gate in schema PR.

alex: cool. let's reconvene next Wed 10:30 for a short sync after initial PRs. :thumbsup:
